headline: The Yamuna promise stack: Delhi's dated commitments
intro: Delhi's water governance runs on announced deadlines - drains to be trapped by a date, treatment capacity by a year, a river 'clean' by a festival. This register keeps each commitment with its original citation and never overwrites a date: when a deadline moves or passes silently, that history is the finding.

status_legend.delivered: Done, with a source confirming it
status_legend.slipped: Officially or credibly re-dated - the old and new dates are both kept
status_legend.overdue: Past its promised date with no official word
status_legend.unverified: A change may have happened; awaiting a citable confirmation

commitments.title: Trap all 39 major drains outfalling to the Yamuna
commitments.committed_by: Delhi government (I&FC / DJB, Yamuna rejuvenation programme)
commitments.what: March 2026 reporting: 17 drains already trapped, work underway on 22 more, with the government's stated target of completing the trapping by 30 June 2026. Drain-trapping is the load-bearing claim in every Yamuna clean-up plan - untrapped drains are how 84% of the pollution load reaches the river.

commitment_source.label: Amar Ujala, 24 March 2026 - '17 drains trapped, work underway on 22 others' with the 30 June target

status_history.note: 17 of 39 trapped; 22 in progress against the 30 June 2026 target

Deadline passed three weeks ago; no known public completion announcement or updated count as of this register's compilation. First DPCC monthly report covering July should show it in the drain-quality numbers if trapping completed.
status_history.source_label: Register compilation check (no citable update found)

commitments.title: Mission Sahibi: dredge the silt-choked Najafgarh drain
commitments.what: A bathymetric survey found ~9.1 million cubic metres of silt on the bed of the 57-km drain. The mission deploys 32 machines including Finnish Watermaster amphibious dredgers to restore carrying capacity - both a pollution intervention and flood-season insurance for west Delhi.

commitment_source.label: ETV Bharat, March 2026 - Mission Sahibi launch, silt survey and equipment details

status_history.note: Launch reported with survey numbers and machine deployment

commitments.title: Rs 860 crore: 12 decentralised STPs along the Najafgarh drain
commitments.what: Approved project to intercept and treat sewage entering the Najafgarh drain - the channel carrying the largest single share of Delhi's Yamuna pollution load - through 12 decentralised treatment plants rather than trunk diversion.

commitment_source.label: Delhi-Haryana Najafgarh sewage coverage naming the approved DSTP project (2026)

status_history.note: Approval reported; no known public tender/construction milestone yet. Needs a dated procurement citation to move to on-track.

commitments.title: Rs 403 crore STP upgrade package
commitments.what: 2025 package to upgrade existing sewage treatment plants toward discharge-standard compliance - directly answering the NGT record (75% of STPs lacking disinfection; 25 STPs' effluent failing DPCC norms per the CAG).

commitment_source.label: india.com report on the Rs 403 crore Yamuna clean-up / STP upgrade plan

status_history.note: Sanction reported; per-plant scope and completion dates not yet public. Economic Survey and DJB budget documents are the verification venue.

commitments.title: Raise sewage-treatment capacity to 1,250 MGD by June 2027
commitments.what: The umbrella capacity target behind the STP packages (Rs 901 crore sanctioned for +51.5 MGD across 8 plants; 3 new STPs; 18 upgrades from 343 to 456 MGD). Context for scale: the CAG's audit-period baseline had 594 MGD generated and 545 MGD treated by 35 STPs, with 212.59 MGD from unauthorised colonies entering storm drains untreated.

commitment_source.label: Reporting on the approved Najafgarh DSTP project naming the 1,250 MGD by June 2027 programme target

status_history.note: Component sanctions (Rs 901 cr / Rs 860 cr / Rs 403 cr) are moving; no independent capacity audit yet against the headline number.

commitments.title: A 'clean Yamuna' within the government's stated three-year horizon
commitments.committed_by: Delhi government (2025 administration), echoing the central Yamuna push
commitments.what: The political umbrella over every entry above: the 2025 government committed to making the Yamuna measurably clean - commonly framed as bathe-able for Chhath - within roughly three years of taking office. This register treats it as the accountability wrapper: its verifiable content is the DPCC monthly numbers at the 8 river stations and 27 drains.

commitment_source.label: Rs 403-crore plan reporting carrying the government's clean-Yamuna framing (2025)

status_history.note: Programme components funded and moving; the DPCC monthly series (faecal coliform + BOD at ITO/Nizamuddin/Okhla) is the scoreboard this register will cite. The 2025 Chhath froth season is the first hard checkpoint.

commitments.title: Renuka, Lakhwar and Kishau dams - the perpetual augmentation promise
commitments.committed_by: Government of India + basin states (Delhi co-funding Renuka's water component)
commitments.what: Three upper-Yamuna storage dams promised for decades as the fix for Delhi's raw-water ceiling. Delhi's own auditor has now rendered the register's verdict for it: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 calls the prospects of augmentation from these projects 'remote'.

commitment_source.label: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 ('augmentation remote' finding; tabled 23 March 2026)

status_history.note: Apex-audit verdict: 'remote'. Kept open because the promise keeps being re-announced.

commitments.title: Wazirabad WTP and command-area rehabilitation (post-ADB withdrawal)
commitments.what: The CAG found that planning failures led ADB to withdraw Rs 2,243 crore of financing for the Wazirabad WTP rehabilitation under the Delhi Water Supply Improvement Investment Programme, and delayed the Chandrawal rehabilitation. The rehabilitation itself remains necessary; this entry tracks what replaces the withdrawn financing.

commitment_source.label: CAG Report No. 3 of 2025, Chapter 5 (projects and works execution)

status_history.note: Financing withdrawn per the audit; no known public replacement plan yet

update_model: Statuses change only with a dated citation; every change appends to the commitment's history - the slippage trail is the product. Delhi's verification calendar: DPCC monthly Yamuna report (~25th of each month) for river/drain outcomes; the Economic Survey (Feb-Mar) and DJB budget for spending claims; the monsoon Flood Control Order (June) for drain works; the Chhath season (Oct-Nov) as the annual public checkpoint on the river itself; CAG follow-ups as they table.
sources_note: Several cited news pages (ThePrint, india.com, Amar Ujala) block automated fetchers but open normally in a browser; the CAG PDFs and government pages were verified directly on 2026-07-20.
